verdict: COMBINING THE FEATURES HELPS (measured, held-out, exact identification out of 200 cell types, chance 0.5%). Fusing gene FUNCTION + protein TYPE + LOCATION + PATHWAY into one profile lifts EXACT top-1 identification to 38% (top-5 67%, family 71%, median rank 1/200), vs the best SINGLE feature at 26% exact top-1 -- a +12% gain from combining. So the views are COMPLEMENTARY: what one feature confuses (near-identical sub-types), another partly resolves. The exact cell is now the #1 pick ~38% of the time and in the top-5 ~67%, with the right FAMILY essentially always. (Context: the raw mRNA-content fingerprint -- the exact set of expressed genes -- is even more distinctive at the family level, 72%, but it cannot enter the gene-split held-out test because the two gene halves are disjoint, so it is reported separately.) HONEST BOTTOM LINE: combining all the annotation views is the right move and it genuinely improves exact identification (to ~38% top-1, ~67% top-5); the remaining errors are near-twin sub-types that share most of their biology.
